children: By Mireia Merino and Gemma  Guasch
Spanish online travel booking firm eDreams Odigeo

said on Tuesday its Prime subscriber base rose to 8.1 million members in the first quarter, as the subscription-led model continued to grow during what the company has described as its peak investment year.

The Barcelona-based company booked cash earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of €23.0 million ($26.7 million) for the April to June period, the first quarter of its accounting year, down 41% from a year earlier due to planned investments.
"In November 2025, we said we would invest this year to unlock substantial long-term growth, and we are delivering exactly," CEO Dana Dunne said in a statement.
The results are testing whether eDreams can restore investor confidence in its long-term growth ambitions, with concerns over slowing membership expansion having weighed on the stock recently.
Markets are looking for evidence that the Prime subscription model remains scalable and can continue to gain traction as eDreams expands into new markets.
The company maintained its cash EBITDA target of €115 million for the 2026/27 financial year and reiterated that it was confident it would reach more than 13 million Prime subscribers by 2030.
